$⇒ 12x - 3x^{2} = x^{2} + 16 - 8x$

$⇒ x^{2} - 5x + 4 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right)\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 4, 1$

$⇒ y = 0, 3$

Area $= {∫}_{1}^{4} \left[ \left($4x - x^{2}\right) - \dfrac{\left(x - 4\right)2}{3}\right]dx$

Area $= {\dfrac{4x^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{x3}{3} - \dfrac{\left(x - 4\right)3}{9}}_{1}^{4}$

$= \left|\left(\dfrac{64}{2} - \dfrac{64}{3} - \dfrac{4}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{27}{9}\right)|$

$= \left($27 - 21\right) = 6$

$

questions.q: The area enclosed between the curves $y=x|x|$ and $y=x-|x|$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$y=t^2+t^3$\begin{aligned} & x=t-t^4 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d t}=2 t+3 t^2 \\ & \frac{d y}{d t}=2+6 t \text { and } \frac{d x}{d t}=1-4 t^3 \\ & \frac{d^2 x}{d t^2}=-12 t^2\end{aligned}$$
So, $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2 t+3 t^2}{1-4 t^3}$
Differentiate w.r.t. $x$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{\left(1-4 t^3\right)(2+6 t)-\left(2 t+3 t^2\right)\left(-12 t^2\right)}{\left(1-4 t^3\right)^2} \times \frac{d t}{d x} \\
& \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{\left(1-4 t^3\right)(2+6 t)+12 t^2\left(2 t+3 t^2\right)}{\left(1-4 t^3\right)^3} \\
& \left.\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right|_{t=1}=\frac{(1-4)(2+6)+12(2+3)}{(1-4)^3} \\
& =\frac{(-3)(8)+12(5)}{(-3)^3}=\frac{36}{-27}=\frac{-4}{3}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.q:
The sum of squares of all possible values of $k$, for which area of the region bounded by the parabolas $2y^{2} = kx$ and $ky^{2} = 2 \left(y - x\right) is maximum, is equal to:

$
questions.subject: Mathematics

Given: $ky^{2} = 2\left(y - x\right), 2y^{2} = kx$

Finding the point of intersection,

$⇒ ky^{2} = 2 \left(y - $\dfrac{2y^{2}}{k}\right)

$⇒ y = 0$ and $ky = 2 \left($1 - \dfrac{2y}{k}\right)$

$⇒ ky + \dfrac{4y}{k} =2$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{2}{k + \dfrac{4}{k}}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{2k}{k^{2} + 4}$

So, the required area is given by,

$A = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2kk^{2} + 4}$ \left( \left($y - \dfrac{ky^{2}}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{2y^{2}}{k}\right)\right)⋅ dy$

$⇒ A = {\dfrac{y2}{2} - \left(\dfrac{k}{2} + \dfrac{2}{k}\right)⋅ \dfrac{y3}{3}}_{0}^{2kk^{2} + 4}

$⇒ A = \left(\dfrac{2k}{k^{2} + 4})$2 \left[\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{k^{2} + 4}{2k} \times \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{2k}{k^{2} + 4}]$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{1}{6} \times4 $\times \left(\dfrac{1}{k + \dfrac{4}{k}})$2$

We know that, $AM ≥ GM$

$⇒ \left(k + $\dfrac{4}{k}\right)$2 ≥ 2$

$⇒ k + $\dfrac{4}{k} \ge$4$

So, area is maximum when $k = $\dfrac{4}{k}.

$⇒ k = 2, - 2$

Hence, the sum of squares of all possible values of $k$ is $8$.

$
